name: Xuanzang
work: Great Tang Records on the Western Regions / prototype of Journey to the West
author: Real history · Xuanzang's own account
goal: To seek the Yogacarabhumi Shastra and other true scriptures
trials: Lost in deserts · snowy mountains · bandits · foreign lands
influence: Direct prototype of Journey to the West · a history of Sino-Indian cultural exchange

name: Faxian
work: A Record of Buddhist Kingdoms / Biography of the Eminent Monk Faxian
author: Faxian's own account
goal: To seek the Vinaya (monastic rules) scriptures
symbolic_meaning: An earlier dharma-seeker than Xuanzang · a forerunner of Journey to the West
influence: Pioneer of the Chinese Buddhist dharma-seeking movement

name: Tang Sanzang (the literary Xuanzang)
author: Shidetang edition
goal: To seek the Mahayana scriptures · to deliver all beings
companions: Sun Wukong · Zhu Bajie · Sha Wujing · White Dragon Horse
trials: The eighty-one trials · demons · temptation · inner demons
symbolic_meaning: An allegory of self-cultivation harmonizing Confucianism, Buddhism and Daoism · taming the restless mind
influence: One of the Four Great Classical Novels of China · an East Asian cultural archetype

name: Christian
author: John Bunyan
goal: To flee the 'City of Destruction' · to reach the Celestial City
trials: Slough of Despond · Hill Difficulty · Valley of the Shadow of Death · Vanity Fair
symbolic_meaning: A Puritan's journey of faith · a Christian allegory
influence: Second most-read book in the English-speaking world · after the Bible

name: Dante himself
author: Dante Alighieri
goal: To journey through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise · to behold the face of God
trials: Nine circles of Hell · seven terraces of Purgatory · ten heavens of Paradise
symbolic_meaning: A panorama of the medieval Christian worldview · human and divine
influence: Foundation of Italian literature · a Western classic

name: Gulliver
author: Jonathan Swift
goal: Sea voyages · satirizing home through foreign lands
symbolic_meaning: A biting Enlightenment critique of human nature and society
influence: A classic of Western satire · influencing later utopian and dystopian literature

name: Odysseus
author: Homer
goal: To return home · to reunite with wife and son
trials: The Cyclops · the Sirens · Circe · Calypso · the Suitors
influence: The earliest 'journey' archetype in Western literature

name: The Buddha · Siddhartha Gautama
author: Asvaghosa and others
goal: To renounce the world · attain enlightenment · deliver beings
trials: Mara the tempter · his daughters · the cycle of rebirth
symbolic_meaning: Founder of Buddhism · the path of awakening
influence: Buddhism's worldwide influence · an Eastern spiritual archetype
